scope: Current SvelteKit documentation with Svelte 5. Remote functions and asynchronous Svelte rendering retain their documented experimental qualifications.

ssr.note: Page/layout options control SSR, hydration, client routing and prerendering independently.

streaming.note: Server load promises stream data for browser resolution. This does not establish resolved HTML streaming equivalent to React/Marko.
streaming.label: Deferred data stream

suspense.note: Async component rendering uses experimental Svelte await support; remote functions are also marked experimental.
suspense.label: Experimental async rendering

client.note: Page/layout options control SSR, hydration, client routing and prerendering independently.

ssg.note: Page/layout options control SSR, hydration, client routing and prerendering independently.

csr.note: Page/layout options control SSR, hydration, client routing and prerendering independently.

serverOnly.note: The reviewed API excludes server modules or function bodies from browser builds, but does not establish server-only UI components whose implementation is omitted from hydration bundles. These are different capabilities.
serverOnly.label: Server modules / functions only

partialRendering.note: Not established in the reviewed SvelteKit rendering guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

routing.note: File-based page/layout and HTTP-method endpoint modules expose route params and request cookie helpers.

layouts.note: File-based page/layout and HTTP-method endpoint modules expose route params and request cookie helpers.

dynamicRoutes.note: File-based page/layout and HTTP-method endpoint modules expose route params and request cookie helpers.

parallelRoutes.note: Not established in the reviewed SvelteKit routing guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

interceptedRoutes.note: Not established in the reviewed SvelteKit routing guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

softNavigation.note: SvelteKit enhances internal links and goto() with client-side page navigation, URL/history updates and persistent layouts. data-sveltekit-reload opts back into full document navigation.
softNavigation.label: SvelteKit router

viewTransitions.note: SvelteKit onNavigate waits for an application callback before committing navigation, explicitly supporting document.startViewTransition. This is a lifecycle integration, not a bundled animation preset; CSS, feature detection and reduced-motion behavior are application-owned.
viewTransitions.label: onNavigate integration

redirects.note: Server/universal load functions supply route data; dependency tracking and invalidation rerun reads, and redirect responses are documented.

serverData.note: Server/universal load functions supply route data; dependency tracking and invalidation rerun reads, and redirect responses are documented.

clientData.note: Server/universal load functions supply route data; dependency tracking and invalidation rerun reads, and redirect responses are documented.

requestDedupe.note: Server fetch responses can be captured for hydration reuse. This is not a general cache for equivalent arbitrary server loaders.
requestDedupe.label: Hydration fetch reuse

persistentCache.note: setHeaders controls HTTP cache policy at the hosting layer; a general durable data cache is not supplied.
persistentCache.label: HTTP cache policy

invalidation.note: Server/universal load functions supply route data; dependency tracking and invalidation rerun reads, and redirect responses are documented.

isr.note: The official Vercel adapter documents per-route ISR configuration. Regeneration is supplied by that hosting platform/adapter, not by a static export or a generic SvelteKit cache on every deployment.
isr.label: Vercel adapter ISR

apiRoutes.note: File-based page/layout and HTTP-method endpoint modules expose route params and request cookie helpers.

httpErrors.note: SvelteKit returns 404 for unmatched routes, preserves error(status, ...) statuses for expected failures, and uses 500 for unexpected failures. A custom +error page is separate from choosing the status. Decide errors in the initial load/response phase: once streaming starts, later promise failures cannot change status or headers.
httpErrors.label: Expected / unexpected errors

actions.note: query/form/command remote functions provide typed server calls but are explicitly experimental and opt-in.
actions.label: Experimental remote functions

forms.note: Page server actions accept normal form POSTs, validation failures and progressively enhanced submission without requiring JS.

assessment.summary: Form transport, validation, pending feedback and optimistic state are separate behaviors; the progressive-forms and optimistic-updates rows review the latter contracts explicitly.
strengths: Page server actions accept normal form POSTs, validation failures and progressively enhanced submission without requiring JS.
tradeoffs: Do not infer a no-JavaScript submission path, automatic validation, accessible field errors or rollback merely from the ability to receive FormData.

middleware.note: handle/handleFetch and universal/client hooks customize request behavior and shared context.

cookies.note: File-based page/layout and HTTP-method endpoint modules expose route params and request cookie helpers.

cssModules.note: The Vite build can import CSS Modules; Svelte component-local styles use its own scoped-style compiler.
cssModules.label: Vite CSS Modules

scopedCss.note: Svelte compiles component style selectors with a generated scope class and scopes keyframes.

tailwind.note: The official sv addon installs/configures the external Tailwind compiler. The setup integration is first-party; CSS compilation itself comes from Tailwind rather than the Svelte runtime.
tailwind.label: Tailwind via sv addon

cssInJs.note: Not established in the reviewed SvelteKit styling guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

images.note: @sveltejs/enhanced-img adds build-time image transformations for local assets.
images.label: Enhanced images

fonts.note: Not established in the reviewed SvelteKit assets guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

scripts.note: Not established in the reviewed SvelteKit assets guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

assetPipeline.note: SvelteKit uses Vite’s built-in handling for imported assets: production filenames are hashed or small files are inlined, with generated references updated. Files in static/ are served unchanged and need manual versioning if their URLs should be immutable.
assetPipeline.label: Vite asset imports

staticAssets.note: The static directory publishes files unchanged, while Vite processes imported source assets. paths.base and asset/path helpers must match the deployment; static copying is separate from content hashing.
staticAssets.label: Static directory / Vite

metadata.note: svelte:head emits data-driven title/meta markup. Applications own deduplication/composition rather than a structured metadata object registry.
metadata.label: Head elements

assessment.summary: Reactive head elements with direct markup control, rather than a structured SEO-field registry.
strengths: Head values can use the same loaded data as the page.
The compiler integrates server head output and browser updates.
tradeoffs: Applications own layout metadata composition and duplicate-tag policy.
Title templates and general metadata merge/reset behavior are not supplied by svelte:head itself.

dynamicMetadata.note: svelte:head can render titles and metadata from page/load data and update them during client navigation. This uses the existing page data flow; structured field inheritance and deduplication remain application-owned.
dynamicMetadata.label: Load data / svelte:head

metadataInheritance.note: Not established in the reviewed SvelteKit metadata guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

metadataOverrides.note: Not established in the reviewed SvelteKit metadata guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

titleTemplates.note: Not established in the reviewed SvelteKit metadata guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

socialImages.note: Not established in the reviewed SvelteKit metadata guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

sitemaps.note: The SEO workflow uses an application-owned sitemap endpoint and static crawler files; URL enumeration and directive contents are authored by the app.
sitemaps.label: Endpoint / static file

robots.note: The SEO workflow uses an application-owned sitemap endpoint and static crawler files; URL enumeration and directive contents are authored by the app.
robots.label: Endpoint / static file

markdown.note: mdsvex is an external Markdown/Svelte compiler. The official sv addon configures that package; an official setup command does not make mdsvex a Svelte-owned compiler.
markdown.label: mdsvex via sv addon

collections.note: Not established in the reviewed SvelteKit content guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

draftMode.note: Not established in the reviewed SvelteKit content guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

translations.note: The Svelte package directory lists i18n integrations, including Paraglide JS and Wuchale.
translations.label: i18n packages

localeRouting.note: The Paraglide addon configures locale-aware app routing and messages through an external package.
localeRouting.label: Paraglide

localeFormatting.note: Not established in the reviewed SvelteKit i18n guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

auth.note: The auth guide points to external libraries and explains session/token policy; authentication is not a bundled account system.
auth.label: Auth integration

csp.note: Configured CSP uses nonces for dynamic pages in auto mode and hashes for prerendered pages. Generated inline scripts/styles are coordinated, with %sveltekit.nonce% for authored app.html tags. Nonces on prerendered pages are forbidden.
csp.label: CSP configuration

cspNonce.note: Configured CSP uses nonces for dynamic pages in auto mode and hashes for prerendered pages. Generated inline scripts/styles are coordinated, with %sveltekit.nonce% for authored app.html tags. Nonces on prerendered pages are forbidden.
cspNonce.label: CSP nonce / auto mode

csrf.note: SvelteKit checks Origin on unsafe browser requests with form-like content types in production. trustedOrigins configures exceptions; this is origin enforcement, not a CSRF-token service, and it does not protect arbitrary JSON APIs by token.
csrf.label: Production origin checks

environment.note: Server-only files/private environment imports are rejected when they leak into browser import graphs. Serialized responses still require care.

assessment.summary: SvelteKit separates private environment/server modules from code imported into browser builds.
strengths: Private environment modules and .server files are guarded against client imports.
tradeoffs: Values intentionally serialized by server load/functions can still be disclosed. Import guards do not replace authorization or output review.

types.note: SvelteKit supplies typed route tooling and the sv/Vite development workflow.

hmr.note: SvelteKit supplies typed route tooling and the sv/Vite development workflow.

cli.note: SvelteKit supplies typed route tooling and the sv/Vite development workflow.

bundleAnalysis.note: Not established in the reviewed SvelteKit tooling guide. External integrations or application code may provide this behavior.

unitTests.note: The official sv tooling can configure external Vitest/component-testing or Playwright browser workflows. The test runners are external packages; they are not bundled SvelteKit runtime APIs.
unitTests.label: Vitest / Testing Library

e2eTests.note: The official sv tooling can configure external Vitest/component-testing or Playwright browser workflows. The test runners are external packages; they are not bundled SvelteKit runtime APIs.
e2eTests.label: Playwright

observability.note: Optional OpenTelemetry spans cover hooks, loads, endpoints, actions and remote functions; exporters must be configured separately.

errorHandling.note: Page/layout error rendering and handleError hooks distinguish expected HTTP failures from unexpected application errors.

serverHosting.note: The official Node adapter produces a standalone server; the guide documents deployment settings and container integration.
serverHosting.label: Node adapter

subpathProxy.note: paths.base and base-aware path helpers support subpath deployments; authored URLs must use the appropriate helpers. adapter-node documents public-origin and trusted protocol/host/port headers behind a proxy. The proxy and server must agree on the configured mount, and forwarding headers are trusted only from the intended proxy.
subpathProxy.label: paths.base / adapter origin

staticHosting.note: The static adapter exports prerendered routes; dynamic endpoints/server actions require another host.
staticHosting.label: Static adapter

containers.note: The official Node adapter produces a standalone server; the guide documents deployment settings and container integration.
containers.label: Node adapter

edgeHosting.note: The Cloudflare adapter targets Workers/Pages with platform bindings and documented restrictions.
edgeHosting.label: Cloudflare adapter

orm.note: The reviewed SvelteKit server/data guides do not establish an owned orm / query builder API. An application can integrate a separate provider or library; this finding does not mean that integration is impossible.

migrations.note: The reviewed SvelteKit server/data guides do not establish an owned schema migrations API. An application can integrate a separate provider or library; this finding does not mean that integration is impossible.

transactions.note: The reviewed SvelteKit server/data guides do not establish an owned transactions API. An application can integrate a separate provider or library; this finding does not mean that integration is impossible.

jobs.note: The reviewed SvelteKit server/data guides do not establish an owned background jobs API. An application can integrate a separate provider or library; this finding does not mean that integration is impossible.

mail.note: The reviewed SvelteKit server/data guides do not establish an owned email API. An application can integrate a separate provider or library; this finding does not mean that integration is impossible.

uploads.note: The reviewed SvelteKit server/data guides do not establish an owned file uploads & storage API. An application can integrate a separate provider or library; this finding does not mean that integration is impossible.

realtime.note: The reviewed SvelteKit server/data guides do not establish an owned real-time delivery API. An application can integrate a separate provider or library; this finding does not mean that integration is impossible.

xssEscaping.note: Its integrated UI renderer supplies this policy. Ordinary interpolated text is escaped; @html explicitly inserts raw HTML. Svelte directs authors to escape or sanitize untrusted HTML before using that bypass.

htmlSanitization.note: The linked security API review does not establish the specific html sanitization contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

authorization.note: The linked security API review does not establish the specific authorization policies contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

rateLimiting.note: The linked security API review does not establish the specific rate limiting contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

progressiveEnhancement.note: Form actions support native server POST plus use:enhance. The server submission/validation path works without JavaScript; enhancement supplies pending/reset/update behavior, not a separate endpoint.
progressiveEnhancement.label: Form actions / use:enhance

optimisticUi.note: The linked data API review does not establish the specific optimistic updates contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

requestCancellation.note: The linked data API review does not establish the specific stale request handling contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

typedLinks.note: The linked routing API review does not establish the specific typed links & parameters contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

searchParams.note: The linked routing API review does not establish the specific validated url state contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

stateRestoration.note: Snapshots capture/restore configured local state across history traversal, with serialization and sessionStorage limitations. Persistent layouts and snapshot state are distinct; large values and sensitive data need care.
stateRestoration.label: Snapshots

scrollRestoration.note: The client router restores history scroll and controls navigation resets through goto/link options. disableScrollHandling transfers that responsibility to the app; arbitrary nested-scrollport restoration is not established here.
scrollRestoration.label: Kit router

navigationBlocking.note: beforeNavigate can cancel client navigation and request browser confirmation for document exits. Browser unload prompts are restricted and do not provide arbitrary custom UI.
navigationBlocking.label: beforeNavigate

navigationAccessibility.note: Kit announces route titles through a live region and resets focus after navigation/enhanced forms, with documented exceptions. Authors supply meaningful titles and remain responsible for app accessibility.
navigationAccessibility.label: Focus / route announcer

a11yChecks.note: The Svelte compiler emits accessibility warnings for detectable markup/ARIA/keyboard patterns. Warnings can be suppressed, and static checks do not establish complete keyboard or screen-reader correctness.
a11yChecks.label: Compiler warnings

lazyActivation.note: The linked rendering API review does not establish the specific deferred activation contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

codeSplitting.note: Kit builds route-specific browser bundles and loads the code needed for navigation. Shared dependencies and component imports still affect what each page downloads.
codeSplitting.label: Route bundles

offline.note: Kit bundles/registers an authored service worker and exposes versioned build/static/prerender manifests for caching. The app owns fetch strategies, updates and offline data behavior; server actions still need a server.
offline.label: Service-worker integration

scheduling.note: The linked backend API review does not establish the specific scheduled tasks contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

notifications.note: The linked backend API review does not establish the specific multi-channel notifications contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

searchIndex.note: The linked backend API review does not establish the specific search indexing contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

fieldEncryption.note: The linked database API review does not establish the specific encrypted model fields contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.
